indication: Relapsed or refractory acute leukemia / MDS after allogeneic HCT
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 positive; recipient HA-1(H) (rs1801284 A/G or A/A); donor HA-1(H)-negative (G/G) or HLA-A*02:01-negative
design: Single-arm phase 1 dose escalation of donor-derived CD4+ and CD8+ memory T cells transduced with an HA-1-specific TCR, given after lymphodepletion
intervention: HA-1 TCR-T (CD4+ and CD8+ donor memory T cells, Bleakley platform)
endpoint: Manufacturing and administration feasibility; dose-limiting toxicity
inclusion_match_notes: Of every HA-1-directed programme this is the only one that wants exactly this patient: prior allo-HCT is a requirement rather than an exclusion, relapse at >=5% marrow blasts or circulating blasts qualifies at any time post-transplant, there is no blast ceiling and no performance-status floor. Two gates are still shut, both from profile.json: HLA-A*02:01 is unretrieved and neither the patient nor her HLA-identical sibling has been genotyped at HA-1, and the trial needs the directional mismatch (recipient A/G or A/A, donor G/G). Single site, Seattle, which the travel-permissive preferences accommodate.

indication: AML, MDS or ALL undergoing allogeneic PBSC transplant (ALLOHA / ALLOHA-2)
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 positive; recipient HA-1-positive (HA1+/- or +/+); donor HA-1-negative or HLA-A*02-negative
design: Multi-arm, non-randomised, concurrent-controlled umbrella; TCR-T given as consolidation after haploidentical, MMUD or MUD RIC transplant. Record now spans the pivotal ALLOHA-2 portion.
endpoint: Dose-limiting toxicity and adverse events; disease-free survival vs concurrent control
inclusion_match_notes: Prior allogeneic HCT sits in the exclusion list, and this patient is six years out from a matched-sibling graft, so the HA-1 product that gets the most attention is the one she cannot have. The donor requirement compounds it: the design is built around haploidentical, mismatched-unrelated or matched-unrelated donors for a first transplant, not a repeat graft from the original sibling. Worth carrying in the dossier anyway, because the HA-1 mechanism and the genotyping it depends on are the same ones NCT03326921 uses.

indication: AML, MDS or ALL undergoing allogeneic PBSC transplant (ALLOHA / ALLOHA-2)
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 positive; recipient HA-2-positive; donor negative for all HLA-A*02 alleles; HLA-A*02:07 excluded
design: Sister arm of the same umbrella for HA-1-negative / HA-2-positive recipients; TCR-T consolidation after RIC transplant
endpoint: Dose-limiting toxicity and adverse events; disease-free survival vs concurrent control
inclusion_match_notes: Same protocol, same prior-allo-HCT exclusion, so the answer is the same regardless of which minor antigen the patient turns out to carry. It earns its own row because HA-2 is the fallback when a patient is HA-1-negative, and the HA-2 genotype is one of the two things profile.json says has never been drawn on either the patient or the sibling. TSC-101 additionally bars HLA-A*02:07 carriers, one more allele the retrieved typing report should be read for.

indication: Relapsed AML, relapsed ALL or MDS undergoing HLA-matched allogeneic HCT
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 AND HA-1-positive (H/H or H/R); 10/10-matched HA-1-negative (R/R) donor
design: Multicentre ascending-dose phase 1/2a of a donor-derived HA-1 TCR-T given with standard transplant
endpoint: Treatment-emergent adverse events including GVHD and DLTs; cellular kinetics
inclusion_match_notes: Two independent bars, either of which is disqualifying on its own: prior allogeneic stem-cell transplantation is excluded outright, and the AML entry criterion caps myeloblasts at 25% against a marrow of roughly 85%. The HA-1 and HLA-A*02:01 gate is identical to the other HA-1 programmes, so the pending genotyping still has to be done, it just will not open this door. Kept as pipeline context on the HA-1 mechanism.

indication: Relapsed or refractory AML, high-risk MDS, CMML or CML (CROSSCHECK-001)
biomarker: Historical documented HLA-A*02:01 positivity; CG1 (cathepsin G-derived peptide) presented on HLA-A*02:01
design: Open-label phase 1 dose escalation, subcutaneous step-up dosing in 28-day cycles
intervention: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic bispecific T-cell engager against CG1/HLA-A*02:01)
endpoint: Dose-limiting toxicity, RP2D/MTD, CRS frequency and severity
inclusion_match_notes: This is what the eligibility-gate sweep was for: an agent riding the patient's HLA-A*02:01 restriction whose peptide target, CG1, appears nowhere on the nominated feature list. Recurrence after HSCT is explicitly eligible, more than 60 days out, ECOG 0-1 fits, and the extramedullary exclusion is for *isolated* extramedullary relapse, which the thigh sarcoma is not since the marrow is involved. Binding constraints are the unretrieved A*02:01 typing and a WBC below 25,000/uL at enrolment, for which cytoreduction is permitted.

indication: Relapsed or persistent haematologic malignancy after allogeneic HSCT (with or without unmanipulated DLI)
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 positive; HA-1H positive recipient; sibling or unrelated donor HA-1H-negative or single-mismatched at HLA-A*02:01
design: Dose-escalation phase 1 of donor-derived HA-1H TCR-modified T cells; withdrawn before enrolling
inclusion_match_notes: Never enrolled a patient; Medigene handed the rights to another sponsor and the record was withdrawn. The reason to keep it is the design, which is the only HA-1 protocol written specifically for sibling-donor recipients at least 100 days post-transplant, the exact setting this patient is in. It tells the board that the post-transplant HA-1 niche has been attempted and abandoned once, which is context for how thin the NCT03326921 slot is.

indication: Molecular or clinical relapse of haematologic malignancy after matched-donor HSCT (GLIDE)
biomarker: Any of a 19-allele HLA panel including HLA-A*02:01 and HLA-A*24:02; targetable minor histocompatibility antigen identified by paired patient/donor exome sequencing
design: Exploratory open-label multicentre study of ex vivo expanded donor anti-MiHA T lymphocytes
intervention: GLIDE (guided lymphocyte immunopeptide-derived expansion; donor anti-minor-histocompatibility-antigen T cells)
inclusion_match_notes: On paper the eligibility reads like it was written for her: prior HLA-matched transplant, at least six months out, detectable relapse, original donor available, ECOG <=2, no prior DLI. It also sidesteps the A*02:01 bottleneck by accepting any of nineteen class I alleles including A*24:02, and it discovers the target antigen by sequencing patient and donor rather than requiring a pre-specified one. The record has not moved since a 2019 completion date and the status is unknown, so treat it as a design to ask about, not a slot to apply to.

indication: Haematologic malignancy after allogeneic HCT (planned first-in-human)
biomarker: HLA-A*01:01 or HLA-A*03:01 restriction; CD45-derived peptide
design: IND cleared for two allele-matched candidates; phase 1 initiation guided for 2H 2026. No registry record posted at time of screen.
inclusion_match_notes: Included for one reason: it is restricted by HLA-A*01:01 and HLA-A*03:01 rather than A*02:01, so the same records request that resolves the A*02:01 question may open a door nobody is currently looking at. No NCT number and no posted eligibility yet, so nothing here is enrollable and the row carries no efficacy claim. Worth a note to whoever pulls the 2020 typing report to transcribe the whole class I result rather than just the A*02 line.

indication: Relapsed or refractory NPM1-mutated AML without standard options
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 positive AND NPM1 mutation recognised by dNPM1-TCR.1 with a monitoring qPCR available
design: Phase I/II dose finding of an autologous mutant-NPM1-directed TCR-T
inclusion_match_notes: Kept because it is gated on the patient's nominated HLA-A*02:01 restriction, dropped down to weak because it carries a second gate she almost certainly fails. NPM1 mutation has never been reported on either NGS panel and mutant NPM1 is uncommon in MDS-related AML with a complex karyotype, though nobody has actually tested for it. A third problem is mechanical: entry requires fewer than 50% leukaemic blasts among circulating white cells and hers ran 58 to 82%. Single site in Leiden.

indication: Relapsed or refractory NPM1-mutated AML, MRD-positive after prior remission
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 positive AND NPM1 mutation type A, D, G or H
design: Multicentre phase 1 dose finding of a TCR-modified T cell product given with standard of care
inclusion_match_notes: Same reasoning as the Miltenyi NPM1 programme: on-axis through the HLA-A*02:01 restriction, off-axis on the antigen. Beyond the untested NPM1 status, the entry criterion is NGS-MRD positivity after a prior MRD-negative response, which is a different disease state from an 85% marrow, and candidates for stem-cell transplant are excluded, which conflicts with the stated curative HCT2 intent. Blast count above 20,000/uL excludes unless hydroxyurea holds it down.

indication: MRD-positive AML in morphologic remission
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 confirmed by typing; WT1 expression by IHC on archival tissue
design: Phase 1 of autologous CD4+/CD8+ T cells transduced with a WT1-specific TCR plus a CD8ab co-receptor, given with azacitidine
inclusion_match_notes: The newest WT1 TCR-T on the A*02:01 restriction, and the freshest reason to retrieve the typing report. Treatment entry requires morphologic remission with under 5% marrow blasts and detectable MRD, which is a long way from 85%, so it only becomes a conversation if some earlier line drives a deep response. Leukapheresis eligibility is looser, and the protocol tolerates a future transplant provided none is scheduled within eight weeks of collection.

effect_size: Relapse-free survival 100% at a median of 44 months in 12 infused patients vs 54% in a concurrent comparative group of 88 similar-risk patients
indication: High-risk AML, MDS or CML after allogeneic HCT
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 restricted; WT1 expression
design: Prophylactic infusion of donor-derived WT1-specific CD8+ central-memory-derived T cells transduced with a high-affinity WT1 TCR after transplant
inclusion_match_notes: The proof that an HLA-A*02:01-restricted WT1 TCR can hold high-risk AML after transplant, which is the evidence the board needs when it weighs whether the pending typing is worth chasing at all. The trial is terminated and the setting was prophylaxis in remission, not salvage of an 85% marrow, so this is precedent rather than an option. The n of 12 and the non-randomised comparator keep the effect estimate soft.

indication: Relapsed or refractory AML and high-risk MDS
biomarker: HLA-A*24:02 restricted; WT1 expression
design: First-in-human phase 1 of WT1-specific siTCR gene-transduced autologous lymphocytes, two dose cohorts
endpoint: Safety and persistence of transferred cells
inclusion_match_notes: The one WT1 handle on this list that does not need HLA-A*02:01, because it is restricted by HLA-A*24:02. That matters for the branch profile.json flags explicitly: if the retrieved typing comes back A*02:01-negative, A*24:02 is the allele to check before HLA-restricted immunotherapy is written off. Eight patients, safety endpoint, Japanese centres, so the row is a pointer to a mechanism rather than a place to enrol.

indication: AML with detectable disease after first-line therapy
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 positive; WT1
design: Single-dose phase 1/2a of a CRISPR-engineered autologous WT1-directed TCR-T; terminated after 6 patients
inclusion_match_notes: Terminated in 2022 when Intellia pivoted to a preclinical allogeneic version, so nothing to apply to. It belongs in the dossier as attrition data: three WT1 TCR programmes on this list have now stopped, which is the realistic base rate for how quickly an A*02:01-restricted slot can evaporate. Entry also capped leukocytosis at 20,000 blasts/uL, a ceiling this patient would have tested.

indication: MDS or AML failing to achieve or maintain an IWG response after hypomethylating-agent therapy
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 restricted; WT1 expression
design: Single-arm phase I/II of autologous WT1 TCR-transduced T cells
intervention: Gene-modified WT1 TCR T cells (Cell Medica)
inclusion_match_notes: Three patients, closed, sponsor long since out of the space. On the roster so the WT1 enumeration is complete rather than because anything follows from it. The post-HMA failure population is closer to this patient than the MRD-directed WT1 trials are, which is the only reason it is not filed purely as a footnote.

indication: AML relapsed after first CR, previously treated MDS, or metastatic uveal melanoma
biomarker: HLA-A2*01 positive by local testing; PRAME expression by central testing
design: Dose-finding study of a PRAME TCR-T carrying an inducible caspase-9 safety switch activated by rimiducid
intervention: BPX-701 (PRAME TCR-T with iCasp9 switch) + rimiducid
inclusion_match_notes: Terminated by company decision after four patients. Its eligibility is worth reading anyway: AML with prior transplant was allowed past day 100 without active GVHD, which is one of the few PRAME protocols that did not treat a prior graft as disqualifying. PRAME positivity required central confirmation, and target_validation.jsonl flags PRAME expression in this case as assumed rather than measured.

indication: High-risk myeloid and lymphoid neoplasms (AML, MDS, MPN, multiple myeloma)
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 positive by genotyping; PRAME expression
design: Open-label dose escalation with a concurrent HLA-A*02:01-negative control group; stopped after phase I
inclusion_match_notes: Completed phase I and stopped rather than advancing, the second Medigene TCR programme on this list to end that way. Note the inclusion criterion that patients must not be planned for allogeneic HSCT, bridging aside, which would have sat awkwardly with a curative HCT2 intent even had the trial stayed open. Nine patients, German sites, safety endpoint only.

indication: Very high-risk AML and MDS around allogeneic HSCT
biomarker: Multi-antigen specificity (WT1, PRAME, survivin and others); T-cell chimerism >94% if recipient-derived
design: Multi-institutional phase I of ex vivo expanded tumour-associated-antigen-specific lymphocytes given after transplant
inclusion_match_notes: Recruiting, on-axis for the WT1 and PRAME handles, and shut to this patient on two counts. Administration requires patients who have *not* had a haematologic relapse after transplant, and a separate criterion excludes anyone who has received or will receive a second allogeneic HSCT, which is the platform the case is built around. Recorded rather than dropped because the multi-antigen approach is exactly what the user asked to have screened.

indication: AML or MDS after any allogeneic HSCT, as adjuvant therapy or for relapsed/residual disease
biomarker: Multi-antigen specificity (WT1, PRAME, survivin, NY-ESO-1); donor-derived product
design: Two-group phase 1 (adjuvant vs relapsed/MRD) of donor-derived multi-tumour-antigen-specific T cells
inclusion_match_notes: Unlike the Bollard protocol, Group B here is written for post-transplant relapse and counts extramedullary sites as qualifying disease, which is a rare accommodation for the thigh sarcoma. It is also the only multiTAA product on this list that is donor-derived and therefore compatible with the sibling graft. Closed to accrual, and enrolment was tied to undergoing transplant at the Houston centre, so this is a design to ask about at a second-opinion visit rather than an open slot.

indication: Relapsed AML or MDS (RAPID)
biomarker: Off-the-shelf allogeneic product requiring >=2/8 HLA match; multi-tumour-antigen specificity
design: Phase 1 of banked allogeneic multi-antigen-specific T-cell products selected by partial HLA match
inclusion_match_notes: Age 65 or older is an inclusion criterion and this patient is in the 50-59 band, so she is excluded before any biology is considered. The disease-state bar is the second problem: bone-marrow blasts at or below 10% and peripheral blasts at or below 5%. The concept is still worth the board's attention because a 2/8 HLA match is a far looser gate than allele-level A*02:01, which is the direction this whole field is moving.

indication: CD123-positive AML or MDS, maintenance after first or second allogeneic HCT
biomarker: CD123 positive by flow (>20% of the abnormal population above internal negative control) at any point before HCT
design: Phase 1 of post-transplant maintenance with tagraxofusp plus azacitidine, starting after day-30 marrow assessment
endpoint: Safety and tolerability of maintenance; relapse
inclusion_match_notes: The one CD123 trial that names second allogeneic HCT in its inclusion criteria, which makes it the natural consolidation partner for whatever gets her to HCT2. High-risk cytogenetics qualify, any donor and any conditioning regimen are allowed, ECOG <=2 fits, and CD123 positivity by flow is already documented, though the protocol applies a 20% threshold that the requested quantitative assay should confirm. It is sequenced after transplant, so it does nothing for the refractory disease in front of her, and maintenance entry requires CR or MRD-positive status on the day-30 marrow.

indication: Relapsed or refractory AML (cohort B), high-risk MDS (cohort A), BPDCN (cohort C)
biomarker: CD123 / IL3RA expression on blasts determined locally within 3 months
design: Phase 1 of SL-401 with azacitidine or azacitidine plus venetoclax across three disease cohorts
inclusion_match_notes: R/R AML is an eligible cohort, CD123 expression is the only biomarker gate and it is already documented, and transplant more than 60 days ago is fine at six years out. Two things to check before anyone gets excited: prior venetoclax excludes unless the last dose was more than two months ago, which turns on the exact date the FLAG-IDA/venetoclax reinduction stopped, and WBC must be under 20,000/uL on day one with hydroxyurea permitted. Albumin above 3.2 g/dL is a hard tagraxofusp-specific requirement and no albumin value exists in the profile.

indication: CD123-positive relapsed or refractory AML
biomarker: CD123 by flow or IHC with no minimum threshold for positivity
design: Phase 1/2 of tagraxofusp added to cladribine and cytarabine after venetoclax/HMA failure
inclusion_match_notes: CD123 with no minimum threshold is the friendliest biomarker gate in the whole CD123 set, and it is wasted here: the protocol requires that initial therapy was venetoclax plus a hypomethylating agent with nothing afterwards except an IDH or FLT3 inhibitor. FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax is intensive chemotherapy, so the prior-therapy exclusion bites. Kept because it shows how a CD123 agent gets sequenced with low-intensity cytoreduction, which is the shape of any bridge to HCT2.

effect_size: Combined complete response and clinical complete response 72% (21/29) among previously untreated patients dosed at 12 ug/kg; overall response 90%
indication: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm, untreated and previously treated
biomarker: CD123 expression (constitutive in BPDCN)
design: Multicohort open-label phase 1/2; stage 3 pivotal cohort at 12 ug/kg/day
endpoint: Complete response or clinical complete response in previously untreated patients
inclusion_match_notes: This is the registration evidence that a CD123-directed agent produces real remissions in a CD123-driven disease, and it is why tagraxofusp exists as an off-label option at all. BPDCN is not this patient's disease and she cannot enrol in a closed trial, so the row is here to anchor the mechanism rather than to be applied to. Capillary-leak syndrome and the albumin threshold that follows from it are the transferable safety lesson.

effect_size: At the 0.045 mg/kg q3w recommended phase 2 dose (n=29): overall response 21% (6/29, 95% CI 8-40); composite complete remission 17% (5/29, 95% CI 6-36)
indication: Relapsed or refractory CD123-positive AML
biomarker: CD123 positivity by local flow cytometry or IHC
design: Phase 1/2 dose escalation and expansion of a CD123-directed ADC; the phase 1b/2 combination follow-on is NCT04086264
endpoint: Maximum tolerated dose and recommended phase 2 dose (primary); overall response and composite complete remission (secondary)
inclusion_match_notes: The single-agent activity estimate for pivekimab in R/R AML, which is the number the board will want when it weighs a CD123 ADC against the cellular options. Pivekimab was approved for BPDCN on 27 May 2026, so for this patient's AML it is an off-label drug with a published R/R AML dataset rather than a licensed one. The trial itself is closed to accrual; the row is evidence, not an opening.

indication: CD123-positive AML, relapsed/refractory and treatment-naive cohorts
biomarker: CD123 positive by local flow or IHC; prior CD123-directed therapy allowed if CD123 remains detectable
design: Phase 1b/2 of pivekimab as monotherapy or with venetoclax and/or azacitidine across four regimens
endpoint: Safety and composite complete remission rate
inclusion_match_notes: The combination arms that would matter most here, pivekimab with azacitidine and venetoclax in R/R disease, closed to accrual. Had it been open the prior-lines cap of two would have been tight but survivable, and the WBC ceiling of 25,000/uL manageable with hydroxyurea. Kept so the board sees that the CD123 ADC combination question in AML has already been asked and is waiting on readout rather than being unexplored.

indication: Newly diagnosed AML in adults ineligible for intensive chemotherapy
biomarker: CD123-positive
design: Randomised phase 2/3 of pivekimab added to venetoclax plus azacitidine against placebo
intervention: Pivekimab sunirine + venetoclax + azacitidine vs placebo + venetoclax + azacitidine
endpoint: Composite complete remission and overall survival
inclusion_match_notes: Newly diagnosed and untreated only, so a patient refractory to FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax is out on line of therapy alone. Myeloid sarcoma is separately named in the exclusion list, which is worth flagging beyond this trial: the thigh lesion will keep tripping protocols written around marrow endpoints. Recorded because it is the trial that will decide whether CD123 ADCs enter AML practice, and because AbbVie running a phase 3 is the strongest signal available that the programme is durable.

indication: Advanced CD123-positive AML, B-ALL or high-risk MDS after exhausting standard therapy
biomarker: CD123 expression from a local laboratory; >=5% marrow or blood blasts
design: Open-label multicentre phase 1 dose escalation of a CD123 ADC, weekly and twice-weekly schedules
inclusion_match_notes: One of the few CD123 protocols with no blast ceiling: it wants at least 5% blasts to read activity, ECOG 0-2, CD123 by local lab, standard therapies exhausted. All of that matches. The caution is the record rather than the criteria, since the listed completion date has passed and the entry has not been updated since late 2024, so confirm with the sponsor that sites are still open before anyone books travel.

indication: Relapsed or refractory CD123-positive AML
biomarker: CD123 expressed on >=20% of leukaemic cells at any point; HLA match at the B and C loci for the allogeneic platform
design: Phase 1a/1b of an allogeneic switchable reverse-CAR T cell platform dosed with a soluble CD123 target module
inclusion_match_notes: An off-the-shelf CD123 CAR with a soluble targeting module that can be switched off, which is a meaningful safety design in a patient carrying a heavy blast burden. ECOG 0-1 matches and exclusion is for AML with *only* extramedullary manifestations, so the thigh sarcoma alongside marrow disease does not bar her. The expansion cohort caps marrow blasts at 30%, occasionally 40%, so she would need substantial cytoreduction; sites are in Germany, which the travel-permissive preference allows.

effect_size: Complete remission or CRh 26.7% (8/30) at the recommended phase 2 dose; overall response 30.0%
indication: Primary induction failure or early-relapse AML
biomarker: CD123 expression; interferon-gamma-dominant immune infiltration associated with response
design: Phase 1/2 dose escalation and expansion of a CD123xCD3 DART molecule given by continuous infusion
endpoint: Complete remission rate in primary induction failure / early relapse
inclusion_match_notes: Terminated for business reasons in 2022 despite a 26.7% CR/CRh rate in exactly the primary-refractory population this patient sits in, which is the single most useful piece of context in the CD123 section. It tells the board that CD123 T-cell redirection works in refractory AML and that the programme died anyway, so a live CD123 slot is worth more than its response rate suggests. Cytokine release was the dominant toxicity; preferences.json vetoes nothing, so that is a discussion rather than a barrier.

indication: MRD-positive AML or MDS after hypomethylating-agent failure
biomarker: CD123 expression on residual leukaemia at >=20%
design: Single-arm phase 2 of a CD123xCD3 bispecific antibody with steroid premedication
inclusion_match_notes: Terminated in 2026 for under-accrual, and written for MRD-positive disease rather than an 85% marrow, so it was never a fit on disease state either. Its value is as the second CD123 bispecific on this list to stop, after flotetuzumab. Also note the 20% CD123 threshold it used, which is the recurring number across CD123 protocols and the reason the quantitative flow request in target_validation.jsonl matters.

indication: Acute myeloid leukemia expressing CLL-1, CD33 and/or CD123
biomarker: CLL-1, CD123 and/or CD33 confirmed by IHC or flow cytometry
design: Multi-centre phase I/II of single or combined CAR-T products directed at CLL-1, CD33 and CD123
inclusion_match_notes: Hits both antigen handles at once, CD33 and CD123, which is the dual-targeting idea the profile nominates. Entry needs a Karnofsky above 80, roughly ECOG 0-1, and antigen confirmation that already exists; there is no blast cap and no bar on prior transplant. The practical problems are location, Shenzhen, and a very small enrolment target with a thin published record, so this is a long-shot option rather than a recommendation.

indication: Persistent, relapsed or refractory AML including secondary and therapy-related disease
biomarker: CD33 expression on at least 20% of blasts by flow cytometry or IHC
design: Single-arm phase II of cladribine, cytarabine and G-CSF with fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin
intervention: CLAG-GO (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF + fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin)
inclusion_match_notes: Every axis lines up: refractory after an intensive regimen, AML arising from prior haematologic disease, ECOG 0-2, and relapse after allogeneic transplant explicitly permitted at 60 days or more provided GVHD is at most grade 1 and immunosuppression stopped two weeks earlier. The exclusion is for *isolated* myeloid sarcoma and she has marrow disease, so the thigh lesion does not disqualify her here. The one open item is the CD33-on-at-least-20%-of-blasts threshold, which the qualitative flow result does not establish and the requested quantitative assay would.

indication: De novo acute myeloid leukemia, age 50-70
biomarker: CD33 expression (assessed but not required for entry)
design: Open-label randomised phase 3 of fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin added to standard induction and consolidation (ALFA-0701)
inclusion_match_notes: The randomised evidence behind fractionated gemtuzumab dosing and the reason CD33 counts as an actionable handle rather than a descriptive marker. Untreated de novo AML is not this patient's setting, so the row is the mechanistic warrant for the CLAG-GO option above rather than an option itself. Benefit tracked with CD33 expression level without a validated cutoff, which is why target_validation.jsonl asks for the number and not just a positive.

indication: Relapsed or refractory AML or MDS, primary or secondary
biomarker: Detectable CD33 expression
design: First-in-human phase 1 as monotherapy, with azacitidine, and with azacitidine plus venetoclax
inclusion_match_notes: Secondary R/R AML is named in the inclusion criteria, CD33 needs only to be detectable rather than above a threshold, ECOG <=2 fits, and having failed alternatives is the point of entry. No blast cap and no prior-transplant bar appear in the posted criteria, which is unusual and worth confirming with the site. The monotherapy arm avoids re-exposing her to venetoclax, which she is already refractory to; the triplet arm would not.

indication: CD33-positive relapsed or refractory AML, de novo or secondary
biomarker: CD33 positivity confirmed by flow cytometry or IHC within 90 days
design: Phase 1 of lentivirally transduced autologous CD33-specific CAR-T after lymphodepletion
inclusion_match_notes: Prior allogeneic transplant is allowed provided it was more than six months ago, and at six years she clears that comfortably; AML evolving from myelodysplastic syndrome is called out by name in the refractory definition. Karnofsky 70 or above matches ECOG 1, CD33 positivity is already documented. The gap is logistical rather than biological, since autologous manufacture takes weeks that a marrow at 85% blasts may not give her without a bridging regimen.

indication: High-risk or treatment-related MDS and relapsed/refractory AML
biomarker: CD33 (target of the engager); NK-cell count >=25/uL or ALC >=200/uL
design: Phase 1 dose finding of a tri-specific killer engager linking CD16 and CD33 with an IL-15 moiety
sponsor: Masonic Cancer Center, University of Minnesota
inclusion_match_notes: Excluded for being too well: candidates for haematopoietic stem-cell transplant are barred, and the whole case is organised around getting to a second transplant with curative intent. Peripheral blasts must also be at or below 20,000 with hydroxyurea permitted, and the dose-finding portion requires living within an hour of Minneapolis through day 29. Kept because NK-cell engagement is a genuinely different way to use the CD33 handle than the ADCs and CAR-T on this list.

indication: Untreated AML in older adults, including secondary and antecedent haematologic disorder
biomarker: More than 25% of blasts CD33-positive; blast count >=20%
design: Phase I/II of an actinium-225-labelled anti-CD33 antibody, with cytarabine in phase 1
endpoint: Safety, maximum tolerated dose, remission rate
inclusion_match_notes: Untreated AML in patients 60 and over, so wrong line and wrong age band, and phase 2 additionally demanded a circulating blast count under 200/mm3. It stays in the dossier because it is the CD33 analogue of the CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning the case is already considering, and because a follow-on NCI combination study is not yet recruiting, so the programme has not stopped. Alpha-emitter dosimetry and prolonged cytopenias are the practical questions if it is ever revisited.

indication: TP53 Y220C-mutant AML or MDS, relapsed or primary refractory
biomarker: TP53 Y220C confirmed by CLIA-approved local testing at variant allele frequency >2%
design: Phase Ib of the Y220C-selective p53 reactivator rezatapopt combined with azacitidine
inclusion_match_notes: Disease, line and performance status all match: relapsed or primary refractory AML, ECOG <=2. Everything turns on one unanswered question, whether the TP53 aberration is Y220C, and profile.json holds TP53 itself as unresolved between a 2019 pathogenic call and a 2026 negative on a 2%-LOD panel with no copy-number read. Note the trial's own bar is a CLIA local result at VAF above 2%, which is close enough to that panel's detection limit that the assay choice, not the biology, could decide eligibility.

indication: Locally advanced or metastatic solid tumours harbouring TP53 Y220C (PYNNACLE)
biomarker: TP53 Y220C mutation; KRAS single-nucleotide variants excluded from phase 2
design: Open-label multicentre phase 1/2 of rezatapopt as monotherapy and with pembrolizumab
inclusion_match_notes: Solid tumours only and it requires RECIST-measurable disease, so a marrow-based leukaemia cannot enrol; the row is here purely as the parent dataset that gave the Y220C reactivator its dose and its safety profile. It also carries the prior-organ-transplant exclusion, which sponsors sometimes extend to allografts. If the Y220C question comes back positive, the myeloid study at MD Anderson is the destination, not this one.

effect_size: Complete response 38% (15/39) and overall response 64% (25/39) with eprenetapopt plus venetoclax and azacitidine
indication: TP53-mutated acute myeloid leukemia
biomarker: At least one TP53 mutation
design: Phase 1 dose-finding and expansion of eprenetapopt with venetoclax and azacitidine; response assessed in the 39 patients receiving the triplet
endpoint: Safety (all cohorts) and complete response (expansion cohort)
inclusion_match_notes: The pan-TP53 reactivator that did not survive contact with a randomised endpoint: the parallel phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS missed, and the programme stopped. That is precisely why it belongs here, because it is the reason profile.json calls eprenetapopt low-yield while keeping the Y220C-selective compound in play. Prior treatment for TP53-mutant AML was an exclusion in most arms, and this patient has had venetoclax, so even an open version would have been awkward.

indication: High-risk acute leukemia or MDS proceeding to haploidentical allogeneic HCT
biomarker: CD45 expression on blasts for patients not in remission; related haploidentical donor mismatched at HLA-A, -B or DRB1 of the unshared haplotype
design: Dose-escalating astatine-211 anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy as conditioning ahead of haploidentical transplant with post-transplant cyclophosphamide
inclusion_match_notes: The rare targeted-conditioning protocol that does not treat a prior transplant as fatal: patients with previous non-myeloablative or reduced-intensity allografts are eligible if they have no ongoing GVHD and have been off immunosuppression six weeks. Primary refractory disease qualifies, age band fits, ECOG 1 fits. Two things to sort out first, that circulating blasts must be under 10,000/mm3 with hydroxyurea allowed, and that the donor has to be a haploidentical relative rather than the HLA-identical sibling who gave the first graft.

indication: Relapsed or refractory AML with active disease, unsuitable for myeloablative conditioning
biomarker: CD45 expression by flow cytometry; 8/8 HLA-matched related or unrelated donor
design: Adaptive, operationally seamless phase II/III of 131I-apamistamab-led conditioning before allogeneic HCT
endpoint: Durable complete remission and overall survival
inclusion_match_notes: The successor to SIERRA, and it closes the door SIERRA closed: prior allogeneic or autologous HSCT is an explicit exclusion. Marrow blasts must also sit between 5% and 20%, against roughly 85% here, so the mismatch is not marginal. This matters for expectation-setting, because Iomab-B is often discussed as the way to transplant a patient with active disease and this patient's first graft is exactly what rules her out.

indication: Active relapsed or refractory AML in patients aged 55 and over
biomarker: CD45 expression by flow cytometry; 8/8 matched related or unrelated donor
design: Randomised phase 3 of 131I-apamistamab-led conditioning and allogeneic HCT versus conventional care, with crossover permitted
endpoint: Durable complete remission lasting at least 180 days (ITT); 17.1% with 131I-apamistamab vs 0% with conventional care
inclusion_match_notes: The randomised proof that a patient can be transplanted with active leukaemia if the conditioning is antigen-targeted, and the zero-percent control arm is the number that makes the case for HCT2 at all. She cannot use it: SIERRA required age 55 or over and excluded anyone with a previous transplant, and accrual is closed. Read alongside NCT03670966, which is the version of this idea that does admit prior-allograft patients.

indication: Myeloid malignancy at high risk of relapse, including primary refractory AML and AML in untreated or unsuccessfully treated relapse
biomarker: None required beyond diagnosis; donor-specific antibody MFI <5000 for haploidentical donors
design: Phase 1/2 of sequential decitabine with FLAG-Ida followed immediately by reduced-intensity conditioning and allogeneic HCT
intervention: Decitabine + FLAG-Ida followed by RIC allo-HCT (DEC-FLAG-Ida/RIC)
inclusion_match_notes: The American answer to FLAMSA-RIC: cytoreduce with sequential chemotherapy and go straight into a reduced-intensity graft without waiting for remission, which is the shape of any realistic HCT2 plan at 85% blasts. Prior FLAG-Ida triggers a case-by-case review only where the patient was *sensitive* to it, and this patient progressed, so the clause reads in her favour rather than against. Nothing in the posted exclusions bars a prior allograft, and there is no blast ceiling, but donor selection and organ-function documentation that the profile does not contain will decide it.

indication: MDS, CMML or secondary AML proceeding to allogeneic transplant (FLAMSAClax)
biomarker: High-risk genetics including TP53, complex or adverse karyotype, IPSS-R/IPSS-M high or very high
design: Phase I/II adding venetoclax to sequential FLAMSA plus treosulfan conditioning before allogeneic transplant
endpoint: Safety and efficacy of the sequential conditioning
inclusion_match_notes: The named FLAMSA-RIC trial the user asked to have screened, and she is outside it twice over: entry demands patients essentially untreated apart from hydroxyurea or up to two cycles of azacitidine or decitabine, and marrow blasts above 30% at screening are excluded. Her adverse karyotype and secondary AML would otherwise have been squarely on target. Useful as the current reference for how FLAMSA sequencing is being combined with venetoclax, which is a question any HCT2 conditioning discussion will raise.

indication: AML or MDS relapsed after allogeneic transplant with measurable residual disease
biomarker: 5-30% myeloblasts by morphology, or LAIP-positive blasts up to 30% by flow, or recurrent cytogenetic abnormality; DLI available from the original donor
design: Phase 2 of interferon-gamma-1b combined with donor leukocyte infusion in two cohorts by donor match
inclusion_match_notes: This is the sibling-DLI handle from the profile, and the arithmetic does not work. Blasts must not exceed 30% by morphology or flow, and post-transplant salvage is limited to one prior line, which FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax has already used, so cytoreducing her under the ceiling would itself spend a second line. An 8/8 matched sibling with an available donor is otherwise exactly the population, and the underlying idea, that interferon-gamma restores antigen presentation on blasts that escaped graft-versus-leukaemia, speaks directly to the late-relapse pattern described in the profile.
